latest_checkpoint: Phases 1 through 6 are complete. Phase 7 (mockup-driven desktop UI gap, plus one backend story) is now in progress: windows-desktop-in-app-dialogs landed first since two other phase-7 stories depend on it (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/dialogs.py ConfirmDialog/confirm(), tested, wired into ManualFlyout's Reset Progress action). Remaining phase-7 work (Labs Dashboard, Pre-Start Gate, Import-and-launch, Lifecycle Controls, Embedded Lab View, Visual Topology Builder, and the backend Image Pull Progress story) is not yet started. The pre-existing gap noted previously (GET /labs/{lab_id}/export not guarded by a port conflict check, runtime-host-port-availability) is still open.

phases.title: Validate and Move Lab Files Around
Add Runtime API and Docker Control

stories.title: Launch Desktop Application
stories.notes: desktop/ PySide6 app (practicum_desktop) launches a MainWindow that runs API and Docker checks off the UI thread via StartupWorker (QThread) and shows a Ready/Degraded/Blocked banner with an actionable next step. Manually verified running on Windows.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app launches on Windows.
The app shows whether the local Practicum API is reachable.
The app shows whether Docker is available.
If either dependency is unavailable, the app displays a useful error state.

stories.title: Connect to Local API
stories.notes: desktop/src/practicum_desktop/api_client.py wraps GET /health and GET /labs with timeout/connection/non-200 handling. Base URL defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000 and is configurable via a UI field persisted with QSettings. Manually verified running on Windows.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app calls GET /health on startup.
The app handles unavailable API responses gracefully.
The API base URL can be configured or defaults to http://127.0.0.1:8000.
The app can list locally defined labs using GET /labs.

stories.title: Port Conflict UI
stories.notes: Backend now exposes GET /labs/{lab_id}/ports (conflicts + recommendations for duplicate-in-spec, Practicum-API-reserved, and in-use-on-host ports) and POST /labs/{lab_id}/ports/apply-recommendation. The desktop app checks ports whenever a lab is selected, renders conflicts in a table with per-row 'Use <port>' buttons, disables Start while conflicts remain, and rechecks (using the server's fresh response) after a recommendation is applied. Needs manual verification with a real port conflict on Windows.

acceptance_criteria.text: Host port conflicts are visible before runtime start.
The UI prevents users from starting a lab with known port conflicts.
Users can apply a recommended port from the UI.
The app rechecks the port after a recommendation is applied.

stories.title: Define Lab Metadata
stories.notes: LabDefinition now includes name, optional description, optional author, optional version, and default schema_version while accepting older specs without optional metadata.

acceptance_criteria.text: A lab spec includes a name.
A lab spec can include a description.
A lab spec can include author or instructor information.
A lab spec can include version information.

stories.title: Define Docker Resource Requirements
stories.notes: Node resources now support optional positive CPU limits, optional positive memory limits in MB, and unique exposed ports from 1 through 65535. Nodes can still omit resources for simple or older specs.

acceptance_criteria.text: Each node can specify a Docker image.
Each node can optionally specify CPU limits.
Each node can optionally specify memory limits.
Each node can optionally specify exposed ports.
The app validates invalid or missing resource values.

stories.title: Create a New Lab
stories.notes: DesignerDialog (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/designer.py), opened via 'New Lab…' in main_window.py, lets an instructor name a blank draft, add nodes and networks, and save it via POST /labs. Unsaved-changes tracking on dialog close is not implemented (not an explicit acceptance criterion).

acceptance_criteria.text: The instructor can create a blank lab.
The instructor can name the lab.
The instructor can add at least one node.
The instructor can add at least one network.
The instructor can save the lab locally.

stories.title: Add Nodes to a Lab
stories.notes: DesignerDialog's Nodes group adds/removes nodes with an ID and an editable Docker-image combo box (a few common images suggested). Client-side checks mirror the API's ID pattern and duplicate-ID rejection, with inline error messages; server-side Validate/Save also surface any remaining issues.

acceptance_criteria.text: The instructor can add a node with an ID.
The instructor can choose or type a Docker image.
Node IDs must match the API validation rules.
Duplicate node IDs are rejected.
Invalid nodes show clear validation messages.

stories.title: Add Networks to a Lab
stories.notes: DesignerDialog's Networks group adds/removes networks with an ID and IPv4 CIDR subnet, rejecting duplicate IDs and invalid CIDR values inline. An 'Attached Nodes' column, derived from the Connections table, shows which nodes are attached to each network and updates live as connections are added or removed.

acceptance_criteria.text: The instructor can add a network with an ID.
The instructor can define an IPv4 subnet.
Duplicate network IDs are rejected.
Invalid CIDR ranges are rejected.
The UI shows which nodes are attached to each network.

stories.title: Connect Nodes to Networks
stories.notes: DesignerDialog's Connections group lets the instructor pick a node and network from combo boxes and assign an interface address. Client-side checks mirror the API: address must parse as an IPv4 interface, must belong to the selected network's subnet, a node cannot have two interfaces on the same network, and an IP cannot be assigned twice.

acceptance_criteria.text: The instructor can select a node and network.
The instructor can assign an IP interface address.
The address must belong to the selected network.
A node cannot have duplicate interfaces on the same network.
Duplicate IP assignments are rejected.

stories.title: Validate Lab Design
stories.notes: POST /labs/validate now returns structured validation results with valid true/false, a normalized lab on success, and field-level errors on failure. The future designer UI can use the valid flag to show success, highlight errors, and block export.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app sends the lab definition to POST /labs/validate.
Validation success is clearly shown.
Validation errors identify the affected node, network, or interface.
Export is disabled or discouraged when validation fails.

stories.title: Author Lab Manual
stories.notes: The lab spec now supports an optional manual with ordered sections, markdown content, and optional checklist tasks. The actual desktop manual editor and rendered preview UI will be implemented in later Designer Mode and Lab Manual Flyout stories.

acceptance_criteria.text: The instructor can create manual sections.
The instructor can write formatted instructional content.
The manual is stored inside or alongside the lab spec.
The instructor can preview the manual as a student would see it.

stories.title: Export Lab Spec
stories.notes: The API now exposes GET /labs/{lab_id}/export, which returns a validated, normalized, portable LabDefinition JSON without runtime-only id or status fields.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app exports a portable JSON spec file.
The exported file includes topology and manual content.
The exported file can be imported on another machine.
The export process validates the spec before completion.

stories.title: Import Instructor Spec
stories.notes: The API now exposes POST /labs/import. Valid instructor specs are validated, normalized, assigned a lab id, and added to the local in-memory lab list. Invalid specs return structured errors and are not stored. The future desktop app will handle the actual file picker and malformed file handling before sending JSON to the API. Product decision confirmed 2026-10-11: a conflict-free import auto-starts the lab rather than stopping at an unstarted list entry; see windows-desktop-import-lab-file for the desktop flow.

acceptance_criteria.text: The student can select a spec file from disk.
The app validates the imported file.
Invalid files show clear errors.
Valid files are added to the local lab list.

stories.title: Preview Imported Lab
stories.notes: The API now exposes GET /labs/{lab_id}/preview with lab metadata, required Docker images, estimated CPU/memory/ports, read-only topology data, and manual content for an imported or created lab.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app shows the lab name and description.
The app shows required Docker images.
The app shows estimated resource requirements.
The app shows the topology in read-only mode.
The app shows the lab manual flyout.

stories.title: Start Lab
stories.notes: Student start is backed by POST /labs/{lab_id}/start. The endpoint delegates to the Docker runtime, updates lab status, and returns structured runtime errors for the future desktop UI.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app starts the lab using the local API.
Docker networks are created.
Docker containers are created and attached to the correct networks.
The lab status changes from defined to running.
Startup errors are shown clearly.

stories.title: Stop Lab
stories.notes: Student stop is backed by POST /labs/{lab_id}/stop. It stops lab containers through the runtime, preserves the lab spec, handles repeated stop calls predictably, and returns structured runtime errors.

acceptance_criteria.text: The student can stop a running lab.
Containers are stopped.
The lab status changes to stopped.
The app does not delete the imported lab spec.

stories.title: Reset Lab
stories.notes: Student reset is backed by POST /labs/{lab_id}/reset. It removes lab-created runtime resources through the runtime, returns the lab to defined status on success, and preserves the original spec/manual content.

acceptance_criteria.text: The app stops and removes existing lab containers.
The original spec remains available.
The student can start the lab again from a clean state.
The app warns before destructive reset actions.

stories.title: View Lab Manual While Working
stories.notes: ManualFlyout (desktop/src/practicum_desktop/manual.py) is a QDockWidget toggled by a 'View Manual' button in main_window.py. It loads via ApiClient.get_preview (GET /labs/{lab_id}/preview), refreshes whenever the selected lab changes, and renders each manual section's markdown with QTextBrowser.setMarkdown (headings, lists, code blocks, and clickable links all supported).

acceptance_criteria.text: The manual can be opened and closed from the main lab view.
The manual remains associated with the current lab.
The manual supports headings, lists, code blocks, and links.
The flyout does not block core lab controls.

stories.title: Track Manual Progress
stories.notes: Each manual task renders as a QCheckBox inside ManualFlyout. Checked state is persisted in QSettings keyed by lab id/section id/task id, so it survives restarts without ever touching the instructor's spec on the server. A dedicated 'Reset Progress' button clears only the current lab's stored progress, independent of the lab's Docker runtime reset.

acceptance_criteria.text: Manual sections can have checkable tasks.
Progress is stored locally.
Progress does not modify the instructor's original spec.
Resetting progress is available as a separate action.

stories.title: Start Lab Through API
stories.notes: The API now exposes POST /labs/{lab_id}/start. LabService delegates to a runtime abstraction, the default Docker runtime creates lab networks and containers with labels/resource flags, successful starts set status to running, and runtime failures return structured errors with status set to error.

acceptance_criteria.text: API exposes POST /labs/{lab_id}/start.
Starting a lab creates required Docker networks.
Starting a lab creates required Docker containers.
API returns updated lab status.
API reports Docker errors in a structured response.

stories.title: Stop Lab Through API
stories.notes: The API now exposes POST /labs/{lab_id}/stop. LabService delegates to the runtime, status becomes stopped on success, repeated stops are idempotent, and runtime failures return structured errors.

acceptance_criteria.text: API exposes POST /labs/{lab_id}/stop.
Running containers for that lab are stopped.
Lab status updates to stopped.
Stopping an already stopped lab is handled predictably.

stories.title: Report Lab Runtime Status
stories.notes: The API now exposes GET /labs/{lab_id}/status. It returns stored lab status plus runtime resource status for networks and containers, including missing-resource errors when detected by the runtime.

acceptance_criteria.text: API exposes lab runtime status.

Container-level errors are visible.
Missing Docker resources are detected and reported.

stories.title: Host Port Availability Checks
stories.notes: src/practicum/ports.py checks host ports reserved by the Practicum API (PRACTICUM_API_PORT env var, default 8000), ports already bound on the host (socket probe), and duplicate host ports across nodes in the same lab spec. Exposed via GET /labs/{lab_id}/ports and consumed by the desktop UI, which blocks Start while conflicts exist. Export is not yet guarded by a port check, so the last acceptance criterion remains open.

acceptance_criteria.text: A host port already used by the Practicum API is rejected.
A host port already used by another process is rejected.
Duplicate host ports within one lab spec are rejected.
Port conflict errors identify the affected node and port.
The UI prevents start/export when unresolved port conflicts exist.

stories.title: Host Port Recommendations
stories.notes: find_available_port() in src/practicum/ports.py scans upward from the conflicting port for a currently-free port that avoids every other port already used in the lab and the Practicum API's own port. POST /labs/{lab_id}/ports/apply-recommendation applies it and the desktop UI exposes a per-conflict 'Use <port>' button that rechecks afterward.

acceptance_criteria.text: A conflicting host port includes at least one recommended replacement.

stories.title: In-App Dialogs Only
stories.notes: ConfirmDialog/confirm() implemented in desktop/src/practicum_desktop/dialogs.py: a reusable QDialog-based component (title, message, confirm/cancel labels, destructive styling) with 7 passing tests in desktop/tests/test_dialogs.py (desktop/tests/conftest.py adds a session QApplication fixture, new in this repo). stories.notes: New story. The desktop app has no home screen for returning users today; GET /labs is already implemented but not surfaced as a dashboard. Reference design: screen-dashboard in practicum-mockups.html. Depends on windows-desktop-in-app-dialogs for its Delete confirmation.

stories.notes: New story. Unifies the already-done student-preview-imported-lab preview data and windows-desktop-port-conflict-ui conflict/recommendation UI into one mandatory screen before any Start, reachable from the dashboard, Designer save, and (conditionally) import. Reference design: screen-preview in practicum-mockups.html, verified for both a has-conflict and a zero-conflict scenario.

acceptance_criteria.text: The screen shows lab name, description, required images, estimated resources, and read-only topology.

stories.notes: New story. Defines the desktop-specific file-open experience for POST /labs/import (already done); a conflict-free import auto-starts the lab (confirmed 2026-10-11, student-import-spec updated to match), falling back to windows-desktop-prestart-lab-gate when conflicts exist.

stories.notes: New story. The real desktop app currently has no Stop/Restart/Reset controls in its running-lab view at all, only Start. Wires POST /labs/{lab_id}/reset (already done per student-reset-lab) through the shared confirmation component from windows-desktop-in-app-dialogs, visually distinct from Stop/Restart. acceptance_criteria.text: The running-lab view exposes Restart, Stop, and Reset as distinct actions.

stories.title: Visual Topology Builder (Basic)
stories.notes: New story. Upgrades the existing table-based DesignerDialog (designer-add-nodes/designer-add-networks/designer-connect-nodes-networks, all done) to a card-based Machines/Network-Topology/Networks layout with no changes to validation or the underlying data model. Deliberately scoped below future-roadmap/advanced-designer-features/advanced-visual-topology-designer.md (drag-and-drop canvas, auto-layout), which remains a candidate paid feature per open-core-boundary.md. Reference design: screen-custom in practicum-mockups.html.

acceptance_criteria.text: Adding a machine shows it as a card with its id and image.
Adding a network shows it in the networks panel with its id and subnet.
Connecting a machine to a network updates the topology view to show that connection and its subnet label.
Existing Validate and Save behavior, including error messages, is unchanged.

stories.title: Image Pull and Start Progress
stories.notes: New story, the one backend exception in the otherwise desktop-UI-only phase-7 backlog. DockerRuntime.start() (src/practicum/runtime.py) shells out to `docker run` per container via subprocess and blocks on the final exit code only; it surfaces no incremental pull/start progress today. The mockup's start/import loading sequences currently fake this with a fixed-duration timer. Likely needs an explicit `docker pull` step per node plus parsing Docker's streamed JSON progress, surfaced through a richer GET /labs/{lab_id}/status rather than a new transport.

acceptance_criteria.text: Lab status exposes a distinguishable in-progress state per node while starting, separate from running/stopped/error.
When a node's image must be pulled, its status includes enough information for the desktop app to show real percentage-style progress.
When a node's image is already local, its status does not show pull progress and moves directly to container startup.
A failed pull or container start is reported against the specific node, with a message distinct from a generic failure.
